content.value_statement: Storytelling products need profile cards that show identity, context, and AI assistance without disrespecting contributors. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured design guidance for Empathy Ledger card components.
actual_capabilities: Defines storyteller card data hierarchy for identity, cultural context, status, metrics, and AI-enhanced fields.
Documents badge priority for Elders, featured storytellers, knowledge keepers, and verified contributors.
Maps default, compact, featured, list, mini, and profile header card variants to visible data fields.
Provides UI patterns for avatars, badges, loading states, empty states, and responsive card layouts.
Describes AI enrichment displays for bio enhancement, quote extraction, theme expertise, and connection suggestions.
Sets cultural guardrails for consent, sacred content, manual overrides, and clear AI-generated content labels.
limitations: The skill provides design guidance and examples, not a complete component library.
It does not verify cultural appropriateness for a specific community or story collection.
It does not implement backend APIs, database migrations, or production data pipelines.
AI enrichment patterns still require human review and contributor consent before publication.

use_cases.title: Design storyteller directory cards
use_cases.description: Create profile cards that balance names, avatars, cultural context, badges, specialties, and story counts.

use_cases.title: Implement Empathy Ledger UI states
use_cases.description: Build card layouts with avatar fallbacks, badge variants, responsive grids, loading states, and empty states.

use_cases.title: Review AI enrichment presentation
use_cases.description: Check that generated summaries, quote extraction, and connection suggestions are labeled, consent-aware, and editable.

prompt_templates.title: Choose card fields
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new storyteller card.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to choose the fields for a default storyteller card. Include always-visible fields, optional fields, and badge priority.

prompt_templates.title: Design a card variant
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design for a specific placement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a compact storyteller card for a sidebar. Include visible data, spacing guidance, avatar behavior, and empty states.

prompt_templates.title: Plan AI enrichment UI
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced product design for generated content.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan how AI-enhanced bios and extracted quotes should appear on featured cards. Include labels, review states, and manual override behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a component proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to audit a proposed storyteller card design for cultural context, consent boundaries, responsive behavior, badge priority, and AI content labeling.

output_examples.input: Design a default storyteller card for a directory page.
output: Recommended visible fields: name, avatar or initials, cultural background, story count, primary location, and up to three specialties.
Badges should prioritize Elder status, featured status, knowledge keeper status, and verified status in that order.
Hover or expanded states can reveal biography, all specialties, and theme expertise.
The card should clearly label AI-enhanced text and show the source story for extracted quotes.
Sacred or culturally sensitive content should be excluded from automatic extraction.
The storyteller should be able to accept, edit, or reject generated suggestions.

output_examples.input: Plan responsive behavior for storyteller cards.
output: Mobile layouts should stack cards vertically with reduced padding and fewer specialty badges.
Tablet layouts can use two columns with standard avatar sizing.
Desktop layouts can use three columns and expose the full badge set.

best_practices: Show cultural background and contributor identity before secondary metrics or AI-enhanced details.
Label AI-generated content clearly and preserve the storyteller's original voice whenever text is enhanced.
Treat sacred content, Elder-approved content, and connection suggestions as review-sensitive design areas.
anti_patterns: Auto-publishing AI-generated biographies, summaries, or extracted quotes without human review.
Suggesting connections across cultural boundaries without consent, explanation, and governance review.
Hiding cultural context, attribution, or AI labels behind hover-only interactions.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design storyteller cards, story cards, profile displays, AI enrichment indicators, and culturally sensitive UI states.

faq.question: Is this a reusable component package?
faq.answer: No. It is a guidance skill with patterns, data mappings, examples, and design rules for implementation work.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: How does it handle AI-generated content?
faq.answer: It recommends clear AI labels, manual overrides, contributor control, and review before any generated content is published.

faq.question: Can it decide cultural approval for a community?
faq.answer: No. It provides interface guidance, but cultural approval must come from the relevant community and governance process.

faq.question: What should teams prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Teams should prepare contributor consent rules, sensitive content policies, data fields, and visual design tokens.
